idiom_name: header field holding an ordered hop list, appended by a wrapper around each processing step
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: reserve one header/metadata field for the history and treat it as control information, never as application data. Every component that processes the message runs through a wrapper that reads the existing list, appends one entry (component name, optional type, timestamp), enforces a bound (keep the last N entries or compress repeated hops), and writes the list back before republishing. Clone the list whenever a message is published to several consumers or split, so parallel branches do not append into each other. Decide explicitly what a many-to-one step (aggregator) does: keep one lineage or store a tree. Keep the entry format versioned and shared, and redact entries at trust boundaries.
code_sketch:
hops = header.get("history", [])
if len(hops) >= MAX_HOPS:
    hops = hops[-MAX_HOPS:]
hops.append({"name": me, "type": kind, "ts": now()})
header["history"] = hops
republish(msg)          # clone hops per downstream branch
pitfalls: Appending without a bound: histories outgrow the transport's message-size limit and legitimate messages start being rejected.
Sharing one mutable history object across branches so two downstream flows record each other's hops.
Putting the list into the payload, which makes diagnostics part of the business contract and of payload hashes.

Wrong move: enable Camel message history globally on every route -> CopyOnWriteArrayList overhead and noisy traces consume resources on hot paths -> instead enable it only for critical routes or temporary diagnostics.

Wrong move: infer a complete system path from a history header when some hops are uninstrumented -> gaps look like a trustworthy trail and can mislead incident response -> instead label coverage and instrument every required hop or pair the trail with tracing.

Wrong move: use a carried history header as proof of identity or authorization -> an upstream participant can forge or omit entries and poison audit data -> instead authenticate each hop and treat history as advisory diagnostics.
